content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to this and have a project where I need to control something using [product_name]. However, I need more outputs, so I decided to connect two [product_name] modules ([article_no]). I'm unsure how to connect them with an Ethernet cable—should I first connect one [product_name] module to the PC, transfer the program to the master module, then disconnect and plug in the second (slave) module and transfer the second part of the program? Or do I need to connect both the PC and both modules at the same time to a network router? Does the router need to be connected to the internet, or is it only used for connecting the PC and modules? How do I set this up? I watched a video about doing this in the software, but I'm not sure how to handle the cabling.

A router isn't needed for normal operation when connecting two [product_name] modules in master/slave mode. You simply need to connect them via an Ethernet cable. However, it's more convenient if both modules and the PC are connected through a router or switch with multiple LAN ports. You can also transfer the programs to each module individually and then just connect the modules together. Be sure to set the slave module to slave mode.
Thanks. How do I set the module to slave mode initially?
Which version of [product_name] software are you using?
[product_name] Soft Comfort 8. What is the difference if I have version 6?

With [product_name] Soft Comfort version 6, it's not possible to create a program for [product_name] [article_no]. You need at least version 7. To set a slave module to slave mode in version 8: Tools > Transfer > Configure Master/Slave Mode.
Is it the same procedure in [product_name] Soft Comfort 7?
In [product_name] Soft Comfort version 7: Tools > Transfer > Configure Normal/Slave Mode.

Alright, I think I get it. First, I should connect the module that will be the slave, configure its mode in Tools > Master/Slave, then disconnect it. Next, I connect the master module, configure it based on a YouTube tutorial I watched (in Spanish, but you can easily find it), make the program, send it to the master module, disconnect the master, reconnect the slave, and transfer the part of the program for the slave module?

The order is not strict, but these are the main steps: 1. Connect the PC to the slave [product_name] using an Ethernet cable. 2. Set the slave module to slave mode as previously described. 3. Disconnect the slave and connect the master module. 4. Transfer the program to the master module. 5. Remove the Ethernet cable from the PC (leave the other end in the master module) and plug the free end into the slave module. 6. Setup complete!
Thanks. Do I need to create the program as a network project? Can you provide an example of how to send a signal from the master module to the slave module, maybe a snippet of the program?
There's a screen video attached.
When I try simulation with F3, the light doesn't turn on.
In simulation, a slave module won't have a status because there’s no program running in it. For [product_name], the slave module acts as an intelligent extension for master/slave operations.

It works, thank you. (I used version 7 of the software and couldn't set up a network project at first, but managed somehow.) I have another question. I have 8 inputs (6 digital, 2 analog) and 4 outputs on both master and slave modules. I used 4 digital inputs on the master to control 2 digital outputs, and 2 analogs to control 2 digital outputs. Is it possible to use the other 2 digital inputs on the master to control 2 outputs on the slave? Can I link used inputs or outputs on the master with those on the slave, or should there be a separate program for the slave?

It seems that the master/slave operation principle for [product_name] isn't fully clear to you yet. The slave module doesn't have its own program—it's just an intelligent expansion for the master [product_name]. All functions reside in the master module's program. The slave module simply provides additional hardware resources. You can programmatically use master module inputs to manage slave outputs. If you use master/master setup, then both modules have programs. Do you specifically need to use master/slave mode?

No, I can use master/master mode too. If that's better, can you explain how to set this up step by step and how to program both modules—for example, using an input from one master module and an AND function with an input from the second master to control an output on that second module? And how would you reverse this, in version 7 of the software?
Since [user_name] has now taken over, I’ll refrain from additional comments.
Can someone assist?
No help was provided. Could you please assist?

For a master/master connection, use the client/server method. One [product_name] acts as the client, the other as the server. The client requests data from the server, and the server sends data upon request. You can set either module as client or server. In my example, the module with the lower IP address is the client, which requests the state of inputs I1 and I2 from the server. The client retrieves their status, and these inputs switch the outputs on the other module. Setting up both modules involves configuring their IP addresses and network connections as shown in the attached videos.
Here's the 'Client Connection.wmv' video.
Here's the 'Server Connection.wmv' video.
Here's the 'Simulation.wmv' video.

Thanks. How do I use analog inputs from a client module to control digital outputs on the master? I typically use an analog threshold trigger to convert analog to digital, but I'm unsure how to use this to control digital outputs.
That's a limitation with [product_name] [article_no]; it can only forward network outputs (digital or analog) to a slave module. For this purpose, you must use 'Parameter-VM-Mapping.'
See the attached example for sending a value from server to client.
